newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares ease, brief rebound expected.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares ease, brief rebound expected.

text.p: The Warsaw bourse eased on Tuesday, extending its last three session fall but analysts saw the market rebounding briefly on the back of strong buying after price fixing and rises in continuous trade.

The main market's WIG index eased 19.9 points, or 0.1 percent, to 17,399.8, and turnover fell 8.7 percent to 172.4 million zlotys ($57.2 million) on all three markets with 42 issues rising, 25 falling and 23 flat.
Analysts said the market was likely to return later to its profit-taking correction, spurred by the bourse's surge by 30 percent since the beginning of the year.
"We should have a rebound at least tomorrow, but it's quite likely that the market would extend the fall later," said Tomasz Berent, an analyst at IB Austria brokerage.
Some chartists said a 45-session simple moving average suggested that 16,500 points would form strong support for the WIG index in the next two or three weeks.

Czeslaw Pospieszynski of Bank Gdanski brokerage, said that according to his calculations Bank Slaski was trading at relative high nine times 1997 earnings, Bank Przemyslowo- Handlowy at eight and trading and industrial conglomerate Elektrim at 27.
He said the overall market, excluding banks, was trading at 12 times 1997 earnings, which suggested its fair valuation.
Continuous trade turnover amounted to 19.7 million zlotys ($6.6 million) with the WIG 20 index closing at 1,778.9 points, 1.4 percent higher that at the regular session.
Mass privatisation NFI units rose 0.9 percent in regular 25.6-million-zloty ($8.5 million) trade and were flat in 39.4-million-zloty ($13.1 million) continuous trade.
